Smart Blood Donor Finder

An Intelligent, Privacy-Preserving Blood Donation & Emergency Matching Platform

☕ Java 11 (LTS) 🌱 Spring Boot 2.7 🐬 MySQL 8.0 🛡️ Spring Security 🍃 Thymeleaf MVC
Presenter Script: "Respected evaluators and audience, today we present Smart Blood Donor Finder—a full-stack web application engineered to bridge the life-critical gap between patients needing emergency transfusions and compatible local donors, with strict privacy protection."
Problem Statement

Why Traditional Systems Fail

Slide 2 / 18

In healthcare emergencies, finding blood is often hindered by:

  • Critical Time Delays: Families resort to fragmented social media posts that lack geographic precision and structured tracking.
  • Severe Privacy Violations: Publicly exposing phone numbers leads to harassment, fraud, and spam, causing willing donors to deregister.
  • Outdated Static Lists: Traditional registries cannot detect whether a donor recently gave blood, is ill, or is traveling.
  • Rigid Role Constraints: Most portals force a user to be only a donor or only a patient.
⚠️

Real-World Consequence

Patients waste vital golden hours making dozens of cold calls to unavailable or distant contacts, while donors face unsolicited calls long after emergencies have passed.

Presenter Script: "Traditional blood requests are chaotic. People post private numbers on WhatsApp or Facebook, opening donors up to harassment. Portals don't know who is available, and they lock users into single roles. We set out to solve all four of these pain points."

System Design

System Architecture (MVC Pattern)

Slide 5 / 18

Processing Pipeline:

  • 1. Browser Client: Sends HTTP requests via modern desktop or mobile browser.
  • 2. Security Filters: Intercepts sessions, validates CSRF tokens, and authorizes user roles (`DONOR`, `PATIENT`, `ADMIN`).
  • 3. Controller Layer: Directs requests to domain controllers (`AuthController`, `DashboardController`, `RequestController`, etc.).
  • 4. Service Layer: Implements matching criteria, role synchronization, and status transitions.
  • 5. Data Access Layer: Spring Data JPA repositories communicate with MySQL tables.

Architecture Layers

[Client Browser (HTML5/CSS3/Thymeleaf)]
          ▼ (HTTP/HTTPS)
[Spring Security Filter Chain]
          ▼
[Controllers: Auth, Dash, Donor, Req, Admin]
          ▼
[Services: UserService, BloodRequestService]
          ▼
[Spring Data JPA / Hibernate ORM]
          ▼ (JDBC / MySQL8)
[MySQL Database: smart_blood_donor]
Presenter Script: "Our architecture strictly enforces the Model-View-Controller design pattern. Requests pass through Spring Security filters for authentication and role authorization, dispatch to dedicated controllers and services, and persist reliably to MySQL."

Feature Showcase

6. Mutual Handshake & Contact Revelation

Slide 12 / 18

Two-Way Mutual Consent Model:

  • Acceptance Trigger: When an eligible donor accepts an open request, status transitions to `ACCEPTED`.
  • Connection Established: Dedicated contact panel unlocks, revealing patient phone and donor phone to each other.
  • Direct Coordination: Parties communicate directly via phone to confirm timing and hospital arrival.
  • Lifecycle Closure: Either party can mark the request as `COMPLETED` once donation finishes.
Mutual Handshake: "Connection established" panel with mutual phone revelation
Presenter Script: "Slide 12 shows our signature privacy handshake. Verified phone numbers are revealed exclusively when a donor accepts a request, enabling immediate coordination."
Feature Showcase

7. Admin Console & Platform Governance

Slide 13 / 18

Institutional Oversight:

  • User Governance (`/admin/users`): View all accounts, multi-role configurations, blood groups, and locations.
  • Account Correction: Edit user details and manage role privileges.
  • Request Moderation (`/admin/requests`): Monitor emergency requests across all cities, edit parameters, and override statuses.
  • Secure Isolation: Protected by Spring Security `.antMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")`.

Data Architecture

Database Design & Schema

Slide 14 / 18

users (Table)

• id (BIGINT, PK, Auto)
• full_name (VARCHAR)
• email (VARCHAR, Unique)
• password (BCrypt Hash)
• role (Enum Legacy)
• blood_group (Enum)
• phone, city, area
• available_to_donate
• created_at (DATETIME)

user_roles (Table)

• user_id (BIGINT, FK)
• role (VARCHAR, Enum)

Supports dynamic multi-role assignment allowing users to hold DONOR, PATIENT, and ADMIN roles simultaneously.

blood_requests (Table)

• id (BIGINT, PK, Auto)
• patient_id (BIGINT, FK)
• accepted_donor_id (FK)
• blood_group (Enum)
• city, area (VARCHAR)
• units_required (INT)
• hospital_address
• status (Enum: OPEN, etc.)

Presenter Script: "Slide 14 highlights our database design. Three normalized tables in MySQL handle user accounts, role collections, and blood requests, with foreign key integrity."
Deployment & Setup

How to Access & Run the Project

Slide 15 / 18
1️⃣

Prerequisites

• JDK 11 installed
• Maven 3.6+ installed
• MySQL 8.0 on port 3306

2️⃣

Database Setup

Run in MySQL:
CREATE DATABASE smart_blood_donor;

3️⃣

Build & Run

Execute in terminal:
mvn spring-boot:run
or run build.bat

4️⃣

Access Portal

Open browser at:
http://localhost:8080
Register or Login

First Administrator Creation: Register an account via /register, then run in MySQL: UPDATE users SET role='ADMIN' WHERE email='admin@example.com';
Presenter Script: "Running the application is simple: create the MySQL database, execute `mvn spring-boot:run`, and open `localhost:8080` in your browser."
Quality Assurance

Testing, Verification & Security

Slide 16 / 18

Automated Test Suite (100% Pass)

  • SmartBloodDonorApplicationTests: Context bootstrap validation.
  • AuthControllerTest: Registration & login authentication flows.
  • BloodRequestServiceTest: Blood group & city matching, donor acceptance constraints.
  • ProfileControllerTest: Dynamic role addition & security context sync.
  • UserServiceTest: BCrypt encryption and repository queries.

Defensive Security Controls

  • BCrypt Salting: 10-round salted key derivation prevents password theft.
  • CSRF Protection: Guard tokens on all state-modifying POST requests.
  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Endpoints secured by role hierarchies.
  • Ownership Checks: Users can modify only authorized requests.
Presenter Script: "Our automated test suite covers context initialization, authentication, and core matching logic with 100% pass rates, backed by BCrypt hashing and CSRF defenses."
